title: Best Auto Apply Tools for Jobs in 2026: Top Ranked
summary: The best tool to auto apply to jobs in 2026 is Tsenta. Compare 8 tools, including AIApply and JobHire.ai, on price, caps, and cost per application.
body_markdown:
The best tool to auto apply to jobs in 2026 is Tsenta, an AI job application agent that submits complete applications for you. It finds roles on 50,000+ company career pages, tailors your resume and cover letter to each one, and submits through 30+ employer systems such as Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, and iCIMS. Your first 25 applications are free with no card, and paid plans start at $19 a month for 600 applications.


That answer depends on what you mean by "auto apply." The tools in this category split into two groups. One group fills out forms and tracks applications while you still click submit. The other group submits applications for you. Below we rank the eight best auto apply tools for jobs in 2026 on whether they actually submit, where they apply, tailoring, receipts, and price: Tsenta, JobCopilot, AIApply, JobHire.ai, LazyApply, LoopCV, Simplify, and Jobright. Each gets a fair entry with prices checked on its own site.


## Comparison: the best auto apply tools for jobs


We checked the prices and caps below on each company's own website on October 22, 2026. Where a company does not publish a number on a public page, the table says so instead of guessing. Prices are in USD unless noted. Daily caps are converted at 30 days a month. Cost per application assumes you use the full allowance or daily cap, so it is a floor, not a typical figure. JobHire.ai has no public pricing page, so its figures come from its own blog and may differ at checkout.

Two things the table cannot show. First, where a tool applies matters as much as how many applications it sends. Many employers post on their own career pages, which run on systems like Workday, Greenhouse, and Lever, and a tool that only works on job boards never reaches those listings. Second, a cap is a ceiling. A cheap plan with a high daily cap can still send fewer useful applications than a smaller plan that tailors each one.


## What should you look for in an auto apply tool for jobs?


The best tool does more than save typing. It should help you apply earlier, reach real company career pages, handle the major ATS flows reliably, and keep you in control of quality. Use the same yardstick on every tool:


- **Submission depth:** does it submit the whole application, or fill fields and stop?
- **Where it applies:** company career pages and their ATSes, or job boards only?
- **Tailoring:** does it rewrite the resume and write a cover letter for each role, and is that included or extra?
- **Review control:** can you check what it changed before it goes out?
- **Receipts:** can you see exactly what was sent, and where each application stands?
- **Pricing clarity:** is the price public, and what does one application really cost?
- **A way to test:** is there a free tier, a trial, or a refund window?


## Why use an auto apply tool for your job search?


An auto apply tool takes the repetitive part of applying off your plate, so you can reach more roles while they are still new instead of retyping the same work history into every employer form. It helps most in high-volume, time-sensitive searches.[New grads](https://tsenta.com/new-grads) use them to reach enough openings quickly. Laid-off workers use them to get back in front of employers without rebuilding the same application fifty times.[International students](https://tsenta.com/international) use them to keep pace with work authorization timelines while filtering for roles that fit. The work usually breaks into four steps:


1. **Find:** catch newly posted roles early with a match feed.
2. **Prep:** generate a role-specific resume and cover letter from the job description.
3. **Apply:** complete the full ATS application, not just a simplified flow.
4. **Track:** keep a record of what was sent, when, and any recruiter reply.


Most tools cover one or two of these. Fewer do all four in one place.


## The best auto apply tools for jobs in 2026


### 1. Tsenta


Tsenta is the clearest answer if "auto apply to jobs" means applications actually submitted. It is a Y Combinator-backed (S26) AI job application agent that covers all four steps: it watches 50,000+ company career pages and matches roles to your profile, prepares a job-specific resume and cover letter, submits the complete application, and tracks the response.


**What it does**


- **Career page monitoring:** watches 50,000+ company career pages and surfaces roles that fit your profile. You pick which roles to apply to, or turn on[Tsenta Auto Apply](https://tsenta.com/auto-apply) , where available, to submit eligible roles within your filters and daily cap.
- **Role-specific tailoring:** rewrites your resume and drafts a cover letter from the job description. Honest mode rewords your existing experience, Aggressive mode rewrites more freely, and you can review the changes.
- **Full ATS submission:** logs in, completes every field, answers open-ended questions, uploads documents, and submits through 30+ ATSes including Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, and iCIMS.
- **Receipts and tracking:** every submission has a record of what was sent, which can include the filled fields, answers, resume, and cover letter, with detail that varies by employer system. Recruiter replies route back to the right application.
- **Seven ways to use it:** the web app,[iOS and Android apps](https://tsenta.com/mobile) , a Chrome extension, an[MCP server and CLI](https://tsenta.com/mcp) for AI assistants such as Claude, Cursor, and Codex, and[iMessage and WhatsApp](https://tsenta.com/messaging) , where you text Tsenta the roles you want, it replies with matches, and you reply yes to apply.


**Pricing:** the first 25 applications are free, no card required.[Paid plans](https://tsenta.com/pricing) are Starter at $19 a month for 600 applications per 30-day cycle (about 20 a day), Pro at $39 a month for 1,500 (about 50 a day, the most popular plan), and Power at $99 a month for 4,500 (about 150 a day). Quarterly and annual billing lower the effective rate by up to 36%. Only successful submissions use your allowance.


**Pros**


- Submits complete applications on the employer systems where many roles are posted
- Resume tailoring and cover letters are included on every plan, including the free 25
- A record of every submission, so you can check what went out
- Published prices and allowances, about 2 to 3 cents per application at full use


**Cons**


- Plans have monthly caps, so very high-volume searches need Pro or Power
- A newer company than the legacy trackers and extensions
- If all you want is a tracker or autofill, it is more tool than you need


Tsenta is built around the real bottleneck in a job search: getting complete, tailored applications submitted early on real company systems, with a clear view of what was sent.


### 2. JobCopilot


JobCopilot is the closest match to Tsenta's approach. It says its copilot looks for new jobs on over 500,000 company career pages and "exclusively applies to verified jobs on official company career pages," so it is not a job-board bot.


**Pricing:** Premium starts from $0.93 a day with one copilot and up to 20 job matches a day. Elite starts from $1.05 a day with three copilots, up to 50 matches a day, resume tailoring for every application, and credits to contact hiring managers. Weekly, monthly, and quarterly plans are available. No free tier or trial is shown on its pricing page.


**Pros**


- Applies on company career pages rather than job boards
- Clear daily limits on each plan
- You can save applications for review before they go out


**Cons**


- Per-application resume tailoring is on Elite only
- The headline price is a "starts from" daily rate, so check the price for the billing period you pick
- Caps are counted as job matches per day, and it does not publish a list of supported ATSes


JobCopilot is a solid option for guided automation on company sites. It ranks below Tsenta because tailoring is an upgrade rather than standard, and Tsenta lets you test tailoring and submission on 25 free applications. See the full[Tsenta vs JobCopilot comparison](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-jobcopilot) .


### 3. AIApply


AIApply is a bundle of AI job tools: a resume builder, cover letter generator, resume scanner, job board, interview prep with Interview Buddy, and an Auto Apply feature that submits applications for you. Its free tier lets you try the writing tools and browse the job board.


**Pricing:** AIApply's comparison pages put its Pro plan at about $29 a month on monthly billing, or about $12 a month on annual billing, with a 40% student discount. Its pricing page does not show prices. Auto Apply runs on credits bought separately: one credit is one application, credits come in packs (for example 100 or 250), and they never expire. Credit pack prices are not listed on its public pricing page, so the full cost only shows up at checkout. Some of its comparison pages also say Pro comes with 5 Auto Apply credits to start and a hire-or-money-back guarantee. Its terms of service say Auto Apply is non-refundable and do not describe that guarantee, so read the terms before you count on it.


**Pros**


- Credits never expire, which suits bursty searches
- Review Mode lets you preview applications before they submit
- A wide toolkit if you also want interview prep


**Cons**


- Your real cost is a subscription plus credit packs, and the pack prices are not public
- Its Auto Apply pages do not list which employer systems it can submit on
- More moving parts to price than a single plan with a set allowance


AIApply is a fair choice if you want a broad career toolkit with apply credits on the side. If you are weighing AIApply alternatives because you want one plan with a published application count, Tsenta gives you 600 applications with tailoring included for $19 a month. Read the full[Tsenta vs AIApply comparison](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-aiapply) .


### 4. JobHire.ai


JobHire.ai is a hands-off service that finds matches, tailors applications, and submits them for you from a dashboard. Its homepage says it covers U.S. roles only.


**Pricing:** JobHire.ai does not have a public pricing page, and its FAQ says prices are shown after you sign up. Its own blog, last updated in September 2026, lists Basic at $49 a month for up to 40 applications a day, Enhanced at $99 a month for up to 100 a day, and Enhanced for three months at $199 total. Its FAQ names the three plans differently (Standard, Pro, and Extended), says there is no free trial, and mentions a one-time discount if you subscribe right after registering. The blog says you can cancel in one click from your profile. Confirm the plan, price, and term at checkout before you pay.


**Pros**


- Covers matching, tailoring, and submission in one service
- Tailors each application rather than sending one generic resume
- Optional manual approval, so you can approve or reject each application before it is submitted


**Cons**


- No free trial, so you pay for at least a month before you can try it
- Final prices only appear after you register, and the plan names on its blog and FAQ do not match
- Auto-apply is on by default, so switch to manual approval or a 24-hour delay in your settings if you want to check applications first
- U.S. roles only


JobHire.ai suits someone in the U.S. who wants to hand off the search and is comfortable paying up front. It ranks below Tsenta because you cannot test it for free and its final prices only appear after you sign up. See the full[Tsenta vs JobHire.ai comparison](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-jobhire-ai) .


### 5. LazyApply


LazyApply is one of the better-known volume tools. Its site says it applies automatically on platforms like Greenhouse, Dice, Indeed, and ZipRecruiter, with a Chrome extension that fills applications.


**Pricing:** annual plans only. Basic is $99 a year for 15 applications a day and one resume profile. Premium is $149 a year for 150 a day and five resume profiles. Ultimate is $999 a year for 1,500 a day and 20 resume profiles. Your plan email must be a Gmail account. LazyApply advertises a 30-day money-back guarantee, but its refund policy limits it to first subscriptions where you have applied to fewer than 100 jobs and the product demonstrably failed to work as advertised. Renewals are not covered.


**Pros**


- The lowest cost per application in this list if you use the daily cap
- A conditional 30-day refund window on your first subscription
- Built for raw volume


**Cons**


- Annual billing only, with no monthly option
- Most of the platforms it names are job boards (Indeed, ZipRecruiter, and Dice), and Greenhouse is the only employer system it lists
- Its site lists resume profiles per plan but does not describe rewriting your resume for each job


LazyApply is reasonable if your search lives on Indeed, ZipRecruiter, and Dice and you want volume at a low price. It is a weaker fit for company career pages and role-specific tailoring. See the full[Tsenta vs LazyApply comparison](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-lazyapply) .


### 6. LoopCV


LoopCV runs saved searches and applies to matches on a schedule. Its homepage says it finds jobs on 20+ job boards and some company career pages, and applies through a mix of ATS form submissions, a browser extension, and automated emails to recruiters. It has a free forever plan that needs no card, and paid plans start from €9.99 a month for higher application volume, priority processing, and advanced filters. Its FAQ lists the caps: 10 applications in total on the free Basic plan, then 100 applications or emails a month on Standard and 300 on Premium.


**Pros**


- A genuine free plan you can keep using
- Low entry price for a paid plan
- You can switch to manual review and approve each application
- Refunds within 7 days if you have used no more than 10% of your plan's quota


**Cons**


- Monthly caps for paid plans are not listed on its pricing page
- It finds jobs mainly through job boards, and it does not name which employer systems it can submit on
- Its pricing page lists prices in euros (from €9.99 a month), so confirm the price in your currency before you pay


LoopCV is a fair pick if you want a free, set-and-forget search with the option to approve each application. If your search is aimed at roles on employer systems like Workday and Greenhouse, it is harder to judge, because it does not say which of those systems it supports. See the full[Tsenta vs LoopCV comparison](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-loopcv) .


### 7. Simplify


Simplify is one of the most polished products in the autofill category. Its free Simplify Copilot extension autofills applications on 100,000+ company career sites in one click and saves each one to your tracker. You still review and submit each application yourself.


**Pricing:** the Copilot extension and tracker are free. Simplify+ costs $19.99 for a week, $39.99 for a month, or $89.99 for three months, with the same features on each plan. It adds AI resume tailoring, cover letters, help with application questions, and Autopilot, which includes 20 auto-applies a week. A credit is only used when an application goes through, and Autopilot submits without a review step.


**Pros**


- The best free autofill in the category
- A clean tracker that saves every application
- Autopilot only charges credits for applications that go through


**Cons**


- Simplify+ includes 20 Autopilot applications a week, about 87 a month, and extra credits are not for sale yet
- Autopilot applications skip review
- Outside Autopilot, every step after autofill is still on you


Simplify is a strong productivity tool and the right pick if you want to apply by hand, faster. It ranks lower here because people asking for the best tool to auto apply to jobs usually want full submission at a higher volume. See the full[Tsenta vs Simplify comparison](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-simplify) .


### 8. Jobright


Jobright is a job search platform known for AI matching, with a job hub its homepage puts at 8,000,000+ listings. It adds one-click autofill, insider connection suggestions, and an AI agent that, in its own words, handles "matching roles, customizing your resume, and applying for you," with every submission tracked.


**Pricing:** Jobright has a free tier. Its public pricing page is for employers, and paid plans for job seekers are not listed on a public page, so check the price inside the app.


**Pros**


- Strong matching that cuts down scrolling
- Free to start
- Insider connection suggestions for referrals


**Cons**


- No public job-seeker pricing
- It does not name which job sites or ATSes its agent applies on
- Its agent page describes one-click applying and does not say whether it can run unattended


Jobright is valuable if matching is your bottleneck. If the bottleneck is getting complete applications submitted, a full application agent goes further. See the full[Tsenta vs Jobright comparison](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-jobright) .


## The best AIApply alternatives


If you are leaving AIApply, decide first what you want to stop paying for separately. For one plan that includes tailoring, cover letters, and a published number of applications, Tsenta is the closest replacement at $19 a month for 600. For a company-career-page bot with daily caps, look at JobCopilot. For a hands-off U.S. service with optional manual approval, look at JobHire.ai. For the lowest price per application on job boards, look at LazyApply. For a free plan, look at LoopCV.

- **Huntr:** a useful tracker and autofill tool. Its site describes filling forms and logging applications, not submitting them for you. See the[Tsenta vs Huntr comparison](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-huntr) .

## Is auto apply safe? Quality and platform risk


Auto apply is only as good as what it sends. Three habits keep it working for you:


- **Check the first batch.** Review the tailored resume and the first applications a tool sends before you let it run. Any tool that rewrites your resume should show you what it changed.
- **Never let a tool invent experience.** Tailoring should reword and reorder what is true, not add skills you do not have. In Tsenta, Honest mode rewords your existing experience for the role, and in the standard flow, with resume auto-approval off, you review each tailored resume before it is sent. Aggressive mode rewrites more freely and may stretch claims, so if you use it, or a similar setting in any tool, check every claim.
- **Watch where it applies.** Some job boards restrict automated activity in their terms, so tools that mass-apply through your job board account can put that account at risk. Tsenta submits through the employer's own application system.

## Why Tsenta is the best tool to auto apply to jobs


Tsenta ranks first because it is the most direct match for people who want a tool that applies to jobs for them on real company career sites. It watches 50,000+ career pages, tailors the resume and cover letter per role, submits across 30+ ATSes, and keeps a record of every application. Its prices and allowances are public, every plan includes tailoring, submission and tracking, with Auto Apply on Power, and the first 25 applications are free. Most alternatives either help you fill forms faster, apply mainly through job boards, or make you price tailoring and volume separately.

- **You want applications submitted on company career pages:** Tsenta, or JobCopilot if you prefer daily match limits.
- **You want a broad career toolkit with apply credits on the side:** AIApply.
- **You are in the U.S. and want a hands-off service that applies for you:** JobHire.ai.
- **Your search lives on Indeed, ZipRecruiter, and Dice:** LazyApply.
- **You want a free plan that runs in the background:** LoopCV.

If you are not sure, the free 25 applications let you point Tsenta at the jobs you actually want and check what it sends, no card needed. A tool can apply earlier and cover more roles than you could by hand, but recruiters and hiring managers still decide, and no tool can promise interviews. The practical benefit is applying before a role fills, without spending every evening on repetitive forms.
